resale_co.name: Certificate of Continued Occupancy (CCO)
resale_co.issued_by: Borough of Berlin Construction Department (Borough Housing Inspector under the code)
requirements: All utilities on for the inspection; lockbox code if vacant
Trash and debris cleared inside and out
Walkways level and free of trip hazards
4 inch contrasting house number visible from the street
Graspable handrail on steps with more than four risers; guardrails on both sides of open stairs
Windows and doors operable, no cracked or broken glass
No pest or rodent infestation
Egress window or door in every bedroom; no bedrooms in basements
Bathroom window or exhaust fan
Dryer vent hard piped to the outside
Water heater discharge pipe ending 2 to 6 inches above the floor
Mechanical equipment kept clear of combustible materials

Smoke detectors working on every level, under 10 years old, 10-year sealed battery if battery powered, hardwired units interconnected and not swapped for battery units; any fire alarm system tested by a certified technician with a copy of the report
CO detector within 10 feet of each bedroom
Wood and metal surfaces free of deterioration or rust; walls intact; gutters and downspouts clean and working
Pools, fences, garages and decks safe; pool gates self-closing and self-latching
Wood-burning fireplace or stove needs a certificate showing it is in good working order
Thumb-latch turn-style interior door locks
All open permits closed with final inspections; unpermitted work must be documented (UCC Bulletin 06-1) before the CCO is issued

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Inspection Application for Certificate of Continued Occupancy (check 'House Sale') from the Borough Forms page and submit it to the Construction Department, 59 S. White Horse Pike, Berlin. The Tax Collector must certify that taxes are current and there are no liens. Inspection requests can be emailed to construction@berlinnj.org. Note that the Construction page itself still links an older (2015) version of the same application without fees; use the 2025 form from the Forms page and confirm the fee.
resale_co.contact_title: Construction Official / Building Inspector (Technical Assistant: Donna Plute)

evidence.quote: No person shall occupy a dwelling or dwelling unit as an owner, residential tenant or lessee unless the owner or the owner's agent shall have first obtained a certificate of occupancy or certificate of continued occupancy issued by the Borough Housing Inspector for the specific dwelling or dwelling unit.

**NOTE** ALL OPEN PERMITS MUST BE CLOSED WITH FINAL PASSING INSPECTIONS BEFORE A CCO CAN BE ISSUED.
Preparing for Your Certificate of Continued Occupancy (CCO)
RESOLUTION 2020 -078 - RESOLUTION OF THE BOROUGH OF BERLIN, COUNTY OF CAMDEN, STATE OF NEW JERSEY, AUTHORIZING REFUND OF RESALE INSPECTION FEE OF $100.

resale_co.notes: New this check: the Borough code (Chapter 256, Rental Properties, Section 256-25, read on ecode360 through its print view) says no one may occupy a dwelling as an owner, tenant or lessee without a certificate of occupancy or certificate of continued occupancy from the Borough Housing Inspector. The section was amended September 11, 2025 by Ord. No. 2025-12 and now sets the initial inspection fee at $200 (including the CO or CCO and initial registration). The CCO application on the Borough Forms page (May 2025) still says $100 initial and $50 re-inspection, so the current resale fee is unclear: $100 per the form or $200 per the code. Because the rule sits in the rental chapter, part of the $200 may be aimed at rentals (it includes 'initial registration'); confirm with the Construction Office. The application has a 'House Sale' checkbox and council reports list 'Resale Inspection Fees'. The same application is used for rentals and commercial properties. Lead time and validity are not published.

requirements: Battery smoke detectors must be 10-year sealed battery units (Bureau notice, 'Effective Immediately', July 2026)
Smoke alarms on each level and outside each separate sleeping area
Hardwired smoke alarms from original construction or rehabilitation may not be replaced with battery alarms
CO alarms in the immediate vicinity of the sleeping areas if the home has a fuel-burning device or attached garage
If the home has a monitored alarm system, notify the alarm company before the test and have the codes available at the inspection

fire_cert.notes: Borough Code Section 162-16D (read on ecode360 through its print view) ties the CSDCMAC fee to the state schedule at N.J.A.C. 5:70-2.9(d), which matches the $45 / $90 / $161 on the Bureau's form (January 2022). Certificates are valid for 60 days from the inspection. The form does not list a fire extinguisher. The Bureau web page still says it is the fire code agency for Waterford Township under a 1996 agreement, but the DCA LEA Registry (July 2026) says that shared service ended in April 2025. The DCA fire directory (survey 5/19/2026) lists Fire Official William Behnke, PO Box 226, (856) 767-7777, fm211@berlinnj.org. The Forms page links the same form at berlinnj.org/berlinnj/Document_Center/Forms/CSDCMAC%20app.pdf.
